mainTopic: The woman who remarried on a false report: her גט, her lost כתובה, and her child, with a side discussion about תרומה separated wrongly by mistake or on purpose
overview: This amud continues the case of a woman who heard her husband died, remarried, and then the first husband came back. The גמרא explains that she needs a גט from the second man as a קנס (penalty), because she actually lived with a man forbidden to her. When she was only betrothed, she did nothing forbidden, so there is no קנס. She loses her כתובה so that it will be easy for the man to send her away. She also loses the rights that come from the כתובה's conditions, and she must return anything she already took. To explain why her child is a ממזר, the גמרא brings a משנה about separating תרומה from impure produce for pure produce. רב חסדא and רב נתן ברבי אושעיא argue about whether a deliberate separation like that counts for nothing at all, or still makes the portion תרומה. The גמרא then works through contradictions between cases of mistakes and cases done on purpose. It ends by starting a question on רב נתן ברבי אושעיא's view, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The later case shows no גט is needed from the second man
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא says that if the second man gave her a גט, he did not disqualify her from marrying a כהן. That suggests his גט means nothing, which challenges the idea that she needs a גט from the second man in our case.
steps.simpleTranslation: The סיפא teaches that if the last man gave her a גט, she is still allowed to marry a כהן. That shows she does not really need a גט from him. If she did need one, his גט would have made her forbidden to a כהן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing a case from the סיפא to challenge why our woman needs a גט from the second husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real גט, even a doubtful one, makes a woman forbidden to a כהן. Since the סיפא says the second man's גט does not forbid her to a כהן, his גט must count for nothing. So why does the רישא require a גט from the second husband?

keyTerms.meaning: A bill of divorce
Made her forbidden to marry a כהן
By inference; this shows that
The last one, meaning the second man

phrases.english: that the last one gave her a bill of divorce
phrases.notes: This is the end of a quote from the סיפא. There she was only betrothed to the second man, not fully married.

phrases.english: he has not disqualified her from the priesthood
this shows that she does not require a bill of divorce
for if she required a bill of divorce
why has he not disqualified her from the priesthood?

steps.kashyaTarget: The requirement that the woman get a גט from the second husband
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the סיפא the second man's גט does not forbid her to a כהן, so it means nothing. That suggests the people-will-misunderstand worry is not a concern, and so the רישא should not need a גט from him either.

steps.title: In the later case people will call it a mistaken betrothal
steps.stepSummary: In the סיפא there is nothing to worry about, because people will simply say the betrothal was a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, in the סיפא, people will say: it was a mistaken betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the סיפא is different, because onlookers will understand that the betrothal was a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since she was only betrothed, people will assume it was a mistake from the start and will not be misled. So no גט is needed there, and the second man's גט is meaningless.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of the משנה
A betrothal made by mistake, which is not valid

phrases.english: Rather, in the latter clause, people will say:
it was a mistaken betrothal.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא shows that no one worries about what people will say
steps.terutzMaskana: In the סיפא people will understand it was a mistaken betrothal, so there is nothing to worry about there

steps.title: Why not say the marriage was a mistake too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: in the רישא, people could also say it was a mistaken marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the רישא too, people will say: it was a mistaken marriage!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer back on the רישא: the same reasoning should work there too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people understand a mistaken betrothal, they should also understand a mistaken marriage. Then the רישא should not need a גט from the second man either.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה
A marriage made by mistake
Also

phrases.english: In the first clause too, people will say:
it was a mistaken marriage?

steps.kashyaTarget: The requirement of a גט from the second husband in the רישא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'mistake' reasoning used for the סיפא should apply equally to the marriage in the רישא.

steps.title: The Rabbis penalized her
steps.stepSummary: The גט from the second man in the רישא is a penalty the Rabbis placed on her.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis penalized her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the גט in the רישא is not strictly needed. It is a קנס, a penalty from the Rabbis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא admits that people would also understand a mistaken marriage. Even so, the Rabbis chose to make her get a גט from the second man as a penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: They penalized her
The Rabbis

phrases.english: The Rabbis penalized her.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גט in the רישא is needed because of what people will think
steps.terutzMaskana: The גט in the רישא is a קנס from the Rabbis

steps.title: Then penalize her in the later case too
steps.stepSummary: If the Rabbis penalize her in the רישא, why not in the סיפא as well?
steps.simpleTranslation: In the סיפא too, let them penalize her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: if there is a penalty, it should apply to the betrothal case too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases seem alike: in both she acted on a false report. So the same penalty should apply to both.

keyTerms.meaning: Let them penalize her

phrases.english: In the latter clause too, let them penalize her!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the penalty explains the רישא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If there is a penalty, it should apply to the סיפא as well.

steps.title: Penalty only where she did something forbidden
steps.stepSummary: In the רישא she lived with a man forbidden to her, so the Rabbis penalized her. In the סיפא she was only betrothed and did nothing forbidden, so there is no penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the רישא, where she did a forbidden act, they penalized her. In the סיפא, where she did not do a forbidden act, the Rabbis did not penalize her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the difference between the two cases: the penalty only comes where an actual forbidden act took place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Living with the second man while still married to the first was a forbidden act, even if done by mistake. Betrothal alone involves no forbidden act, so there is nothing to penalize.

keyTerms.meaning: She did a forbidden act

steps.whatToRemember: The גט from the second man in the רישא is a קנס, given only because she actually did something forbidden. In the betrothal case of the סיפא there is no קנס.

phrases.english: In the first clause, where she did a forbidden act
they penalized her.
In the latter clause, where she did not do a forbidden act
the Rabbis did not penalize her.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The penalty should apply to both cases
steps.terutzMaskana: A penalty applies only where she actually did a forbidden act

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: she has no כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next ruling of the משנה: this woman gets no כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: She has no כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה. This quote sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that, besides having to leave both men, she also loses her כתובה money. The reason has not been given yet.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract, and the money promised to the wife in it

phrases.english: She has no marriage contract payment.

steps.title: Why she loses her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The Rabbis created the כתובה so a husband would not find it easy to divorce his wife. Here they want it to be easy for him to send her away.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason the Rabbis set up a כתובה for her? So that it will not be easy in his eyes to divorce her. But this woman, let it be easy in his eyes to divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the משנה's ruling by looking at why the Rabbis made the כתובה in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, having to pay the כתובה holds a husband back from a quick divorce. Here the marriage is forbidden and must end, so the Rabbis removed that obstacle.

keyTerms.meaning: They set up, made a rule
Easy, or unimportant, in his eyes
To send her away, meaning divorce her

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the כתובה is a protection the Rabbis set up for a purpose. When that purpose works against what should happen, they take it away.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא תַּקִּינוּ לַהּ רַבָּנַן כְּתוּבָּה,
phrases.english: What is the reason the Rabbis set up a marriage contract for her?
So that it will not be easy
in his eyes to divorce her
This one, let it be easy in his eyes to divorce her.
phrases.notes: "This one" is the woman from our משנה. Here the Rabbis want him to send her away.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא תַּקִּינוּ לַהּ רַבָּנַן כְּתוּבָּה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does she lose her כתובה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כתובה exists to make divorce hard. Here divorce should be easy, so it is taken away.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: no produce, support, or worn clothes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה: she also gets no produce, no food support, and no worn-out clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: She has no produce, no food support, and no worn-out clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another ruling from the משנה. This sets up the short explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are extra rights a wife normally has during or after marriage. The משנה says she loses all of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce or profits from her property
Food support
Worn-out clothes or items she brought into the marriage

phrases.english: She has no profits
and no sustenance and no worn clothes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לָהּ פֵּירוֹת וְלֹא מְזוֹנוֹת וְלֹא בְּלָאוֹת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She loses the produce, food support, and worn clothes

steps.title: The כתובה's conditions are like the כתובה itself
steps.stepSummary: These rights come from the conditions of the כתובה, and those conditions are treated like the כתובה itself. Since she loses the כתובה, she loses them too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The conditions of the כתובה are like the כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why she loses these extra rights: they are part of the כתובה package.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rights to produce, food support, and worn clothes are not separate gifts. They come from the כתובה's conditions, so when the כתובה is taken away, they go with it.

keyTerms.meaning: The conditions that come with the כתובה
Is like, is treated as

steps.whatToRemember: She loses her כתובה so the Rabbis make it easy for him to divorce her. She loses all the rights that come from the כתובה's conditions, because they are treated like the כתובה itself.

phrases.english: The stipulations of the marriage contract are like the marriage contract.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does she lose the produce, food support, and worn clothes?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: These come from the כתובה's conditions, which follow the כתובה itself.

steps.title: She must return what she took from either man
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next ruling of the משנה: if she took anything from either husband, she must give it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she took anything from this man or from that man, she must return it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה so it can discuss it. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps before this said she has no כתובה and no rights from the conditions of the כתובה. This line adds that even what she already holds must be returned.

keyTerms.meaning: She took
From this one and from that one, meaning from either husband

phrases.english: If she took from this one or from that one [she must return it].
phrases.notes: The words in brackets, 'she must return it,' come from the משנה itself. The גמרא only quotes the opening words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the rulings of the משנה after the conditions of the כתובה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything she took from either husband must be returned.

steps.title: Why say something so obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say this, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה bothers to teach this. She has no right to these things, so of course she gives them back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 already said she loses the כתובה and its conditions. If she has no right to them, returning them seems to follow automatically, so this line looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. Used to ask why a source needed to teach something

phrases.english: It is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the ruling just quoted is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The line in the משנה that says she must return what she took
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since she has no right to these items, returning them seems obvious and not worth teaching.

steps.title: Grabbing it first does not let her keep it
steps.stepSummary: Without this line, we might have thought that once she already holds the items, the court leaves them with her. The משנה teaches that she must return them anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that since she already took hold of it, we do not take it away from her. So the משנה teaches us that we do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the line is needed. Without it, we might think that once she already has the items, we do not take them away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Losing the כתובה is a penalty, and you might think a penalty only stops her from collecting more, not from keeping what she already holds. The משנה teaches that she must give back even what is already in her hands.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said. Introduces a mistaken idea that the source comes to rule out
She seized it, she took hold of it
We take out, we take away
It teaches us. Introduces the new point the source is making

phrases.english: You might have said:
Since she seized it, we do not take it away from her,
So it teaches us [that we do take it away].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פְּשִׁיטָא challenge by showing the line teaches something new.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the line is needed to rule out a reasonable mistake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once she has already taken the items, the court would leave them with her.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even items she already holds are taken back from her.
steps.whatToRemember: The woman who remarried in error loses everything. She cannot even keep what she already took.

steps.title: The child is a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ruling of the משנה that a child born to her from either man is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next ruling of the משנה. It is setting up a longer discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a strong ruling, because she acted based on a court's permission or on witnesses. To deal with it, the גמרא first brings a background discussion from the laws of תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: A child, offspring
A child born from a forbidden relationship, who has restrictions on whom he may marry

phrases.english: The child is a ממזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next ruling of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child born to her from either man is a ממזר.

steps.title: A משנה about תרומה from impure produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from תרומות. One may not separate תרומה from impure produce to cover pure produce. If he did it by mistake, it counts. If he did it on purpose, he has done nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: one may not separate תרומה from impure produce for pure produce. If he did so by mistake, his תרומה is תרומה. If he did it on purpose, he has done nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in a different משנה as background. It is setting up a discussion that will help with the ממזר ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes a difference between doing it by mistake (שוגג) and doing it on purpose (מזיד). The phrase 'he has done nothing' is unclear, and the next steps try to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: Separating תְּרוּמָה, the portion of produce given to a כֹּהֵן
Ritually impure / ritually pure
By mistake, without knowing
On purpose, knowingly

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in תרומות, chapter 2.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין תּוֹרְמִין מִן הַטָּמֵא עַל הַטָּהוֹר,
phrases.english: One may not separate תרומה from impure produce for pure produce,
And if he separated by mistake, his תרומה is תרומה,
If on purpose, he has done nothing at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside משנה as background for the ממזר ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תרומה separated from impure produce by mistake counts. If it was done on purpose, he has done nothing.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא forgot about the ממזר. This is a side discussion it brings first, and it will connect back later.

steps.title: What does 'he has done nothing' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly the phrase 'he has done nothing' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'he has done nothing' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the unclear phrase in the משנה. This opens a disagreement between two אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase could mean two things. It might mean nothing happened at all, or only that the rest of his produce was not fixed. The answers that follow take different sides.

keyTerms.meaning: What, what does it mean
He has done nothing at all

phrases.english: What does 'he has done nothing' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the last phrase of the quoted משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How far 'he has done nothing' reaches: whether the separated portion is still תרומה or not.

steps.title: רב חסדא: Nothing at all happened
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says it means completely nothing. Even the portion he set aside goes back to being untithed produce (טבל).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: he has done nothing at all. Even that portion he set aside goes back to being טבל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers that the act counts for nothing at all. Even the piece he set aside is not תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב חסדא's view, the whole act is ignored. The separated portion has no holiness, and everything stays טבל as before.

keyTerms.meaning: At all, completely
A measure of produce, here the portion he set aside
Produce from which תְּרוּמָה and tithes have not yet been taken

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא עָשָׂה וְלֹא כְּלוּם כׇּל עִיקָּר,
phrases.english: He has done nothing at all, completely,
So that even that measure of produce goes back to being טבל.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The act is completely ignored. Even the separated portion is not תרומה.

steps.title: רב נתן ברבי אושעיא: It is תרומה, but the rest is not fixed
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן ברבי אושעיא says 'nothing' only means the rest of his produce is not fixed. The portion he separated really is תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נתן ברבי אושעיא said: 'he has done nothing' as far as fixing the rest of the produce, but the portion he set aside is תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a narrower reading. The piece he set aside is holy as תרומה, but he must still separate תרומה again for the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the act does work partly. The separated portion becomes תרומה, but it does not make the remaining produce permitted to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: To fix, to make produce permitted by separating its portions
The remaining produce

phrases.english: Rav Natan son of Rabbi Oshaya said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא עָשָׂה וְלֹא כְלוּם — לְתַקֵּן אֶת הַשִּׁירַיִם,
phrases.english: He has done nothing as far as fixing the remaining produce,
But it is תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, competing answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The separated portion is תרומה, but the remaining produce is still not fixed.

steps.title: Why רב חסדא rejects that view
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא did not accept רב נתן's view. If the portion counts as תרומה, the owner might be careless and never separate תרומה again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא did not say like רב נתן ברבי אושעיא. If you say it is תרומה, sometimes he will be careless and not separate again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב חסדא disagrees. He is worried that calling it תרומה will make people forget to separate again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the separated portion is real תרומה, the owner may think he is done and eat the rest as טבל. So רב חסדא treats the whole act as nothing, so the owner knows he must start over.

keyTerms.meaning: Sometimes
Was careless, neglected
Separates (a portion of produce)

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב נָתָן בְּרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda did not say like Rav Natan son of Rabbi Oshaya,
Because if you say it is תרומה,
Sometimes he will be careless and not separate [again].

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב נָתָן בְּרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for רב חסדא's position over רב נתן's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב חסדא fears that if the portion counts as תרומה, the owner will neglect to separate again.

steps.title: Challenge from the bitter cucumber
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא's worry from another משנה. If someone separates a cucumber that turns out bitter, or a melon that turns out spoiled, it is תרומה and he must separate again. There is no worry there that he will forget.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from what we learned: one who separates a cucumber as תרומה and it is found bitter, or a melon and it is found spoiled, it is תרומה, and he must go back and separate again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's reasoning with a case where the portion is תרומה and yet he must separate again. There the Rabbis did not worry he would be careless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the cucumber case, the portion counts as תרומה and he still has to separate again, which is exactly רב נתן's model. If the worry about carelessness does not stop it there, why should it stop it in the case of impure produce?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Used to challenge by comparing two cases
A kind of cucumber
A melon
Spoiled, rotten

phrases.english: How is it different from what we learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in תרומות, chapter 3.

phrases.english: One who separates a cucumber as תרומה and it is found bitter,
Or a melon and it is found spoiled —
It is תרומה, and he must go back and separate again!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given for רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's worry that if the portion counts as תרומה, the owner will be careless and not separate again
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the cucumber case, the portion is תרומה and he must separate again, with no such worry. So the worry should not apply to impure produce either.

steps.title: A mistake is different from doing it on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the cucumber case was a mistake, so no sin was done. Separating from impure produce on purpose is a sin, so the Rabbis penalized him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are you comparing a mistake to doing it on purpose? One who did it by mistake did nothing forbidden. One who did it on purpose did something forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two cases are not alike. The cucumber case was an honest mistake, while the impure-produce case was done on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person who made a mistake did nothing wrong, so the Rabbis did not penalize him and let the portion be תרומה. The person who did it on purpose sinned, so the Rabbis made the whole act count for nothing, as רב חסדא says.

keyTerms.meaning: You are throwing one against the other, comparing to raise a contradiction
Something forbidden, a sin
Did, committed

phrases.english: Are you comparing a mistake to doing it on purpose?
One who did it by mistake did nothing forbidden,
One who did it on purpose is doing something forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the cucumber challenge by showing the two cases are different.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the cases are different: a mistake versus a sin done on purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cucumber case shows we do not worry that he will neglect to separate again, so רב חסדא's worry fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Rabbis penalize only the one who sinned on purpose, by making his act count for nothing. The one who made a mistake is not penalized.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב חסדא, one who separates תרומה from impure produce on purpose is penalized: his act counts for nothing at all. One who did it by mistake is not penalized.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that the Rabbis penalize someone who sinned on purpose by canceling his act is the background the גמרא is building toward the ruling that the child is a ממזר.

steps.title: Two mistake cases seem to clash
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא contrasts our משנה, where a mistaken separation from impure produce is fully valid תרומה, with the bitter cucumber case, where the person must separate again.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא pointed out a contradiction between one mistake case and another. Here it teaches that if he did it by mistake, his תרומה is תרומה. But there it teaches that it is תרומה and he must separate again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets two mistake (שוגג) cases side by side and asks why they end differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our case, a person who separates impure produce for pure by mistake has valid תרומה and nothing more is said. In the bitter cucumber case from step 20, the separation also counts, yet he must separate again. Both are honest mistakes, so why does only one need a redo?

keyTerms.meaning: And he contrasted: the גמרא sets two sources against each other
Someone who acts by mistake, without knowing
Here (our case) / there (the other case)
And he must go back and separate תרומה again

steps.confusionAlert: Step 21 used the cucumber case to show a mistake. Now the גמרא asks a new question: why do two mistake cases get different results?

phrases.english: And he contrasted one mistake case with another mistake case:
Here it teaches: by mistake, his תרומה is תרומה,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is our case, separating impure produce for pure. Nothing is said about redoing it.

phrases.english: There it teaches: it is תרומה, and he must go back and separate again!
phrases.notes: 'There' is the bitter cucumber or spoiled melon case from step 20.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 21 called the cucumber case a mistake. This step compares it with the other mistake case, our impure-for-pure case, and finds they don't match.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a mistaken separation of impure for pure is valid תרומה with no redo
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both cases are mistakes, but only the cucumber case requires separating again. The rulings look inconsistent.

steps.title: The cucumber mistake is almost on purpose
steps.stepSummary: The cucumber case is a mistake that is close to on purpose, because he should have tasted it first, so he is told to separate again.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the mistake is close to doing it on purpose, because he should have tasted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by showing that the two mistakes are not equally innocent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a cucumber, checking was easy: one taste would have shown it was bitter. Not checking makes him almost careless on purpose, so the Rabbis require him to separate again. In the impure-for-pure case he may not have been able to tell, so his mistake is a true mistake and no redo is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Close to doing it on purpose
Someone who acts on purpose, knowingly
Because he should have
To taste it

phrases.english: There, it is a mistake that is close to on purpose,
because he should have tasted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 22 by showing the two mistake cases are not the same kind of mistake.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: one mistake was preventable, the other was not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every mistake is the same, so both cases should get the same ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: A mistake he could easily have avoided by tasting is treated almost like on purpose, so he must separate again. An honest mistake needs no redo.

steps.title: Two on-purpose cases seem to clash
steps.stepSummary: Our ruling says an on-purpose separation from impure produce does nothing, but a משנה says separating from an unholed pot for a holed pot on purpose still makes תרומה, with a redo.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא also contrasted one on-purpose case with another. Here it teaches that on purpose, he has done nothing. But there we learned: one who separates תרומה from produce in a pot without a hole for produce in a pot with a hole, it is תרומה, and he must separate again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second contradiction, this time between two on-purpose (מזיד) cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following רב חסדא in step 17, an on-purpose separation of impure for pure is worth nothing at all. Yet in the pot case, even a deliberate wrong separation still counts as תרומה, and the person is simply told to separate again. Why not use the same softer penalty in our case?

keyTerms.meaning: He has done nothing; the act has no effect
A pot with a hole, so it counts as connected to the ground
A pot without a hole; what grows in it does not need תרומה from the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: In the pot case, he separates from produce that does not need תרומה from the Torah for produce that does. So his separation is not good enough for the Torah, yet it still has the status of תרומה.

phrases.english: And he contrasted one on-purpose case with another on-purpose case:

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא קָתָנֵי: בְּמֵזִיד לֹא עָשָׂה כְּלוּם,
phrases.english: Here it teaches: on purpose, he has done nothing,
phrases.notes: This is the line that רב חסדא read as 'completely nothing' in step 17.

phrases.english: There we learned: one who separates תרומה from produce in a pot without a hole
for produce in a pot with a hole: it is תרומה, and he must go back and separate again!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the mistake contradiction, the גמרא turns to a parallel contradiction between on-purpose cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that an on-purpose separation of impure for pure does nothing at all
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the pot case, a deliberate wrong separation still counts as תרומה with a redo. So why is our on-purpose case totally worthless?

steps.title: With two pots he will obey; with one kind he will not
steps.stepSummary: With two different pots, the person will listen when told to separate again. In the impure-for-pure case the produce looks like one kind, so he won't listen. That is why the Rabbis made his separation worthless.
steps.simpleTranslation: With two vessels, he listens. With one vessel, he does not listen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second contradiction by looking at whether the person will actually obey an order to separate again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the pot case, the two pots are clearly different, so he understands why he must separate again and will do it. Impure and pure produce look the same, like produce from a single vessel. If his separation counted, he would ignore the order to redo it. So the Rabbis made it count for nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: With two vessels
With one vessel
He listens, he obeys

steps.whatToRemember: Both contradictions are answered by showing the cases are different. A mistake you could easily have avoided (not tasting) is treated almost like on purpose. And an on-purpose case only gets the softer ruling, 'it is תרומה, separate again,' when we can trust the person to obey.
steps.whyThisMatters: This supports רב חסדא's worry from step 19: the Rabbis shape the penalty based on whether the person will actually go back and separate correctly.

phrases.english: With two vessels, he listens,
phrases.notes: The holed and unholed pots are clearly different, so he sees the reason and will separate again.

phrases.english: with one vessel, he does not listen.
phrases.notes: Impure and pure produce look the same, as if from one vessel, so he won't take the order to redo seriously.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 24 by showing why the softer penalty works in the pot case but not in ours.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by whether the person will obey
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All on-purpose wrong separations should get the same penalty: valid תרומה plus a redo.
steps.terutzMaskana: Where the difference is easy to see (two pots), he will obey a redo, so the separation counts. Where the produce looks the same, he won't obey, so the Rabbis made the separation worth nothing.

steps.title: Setting up a challenge against רב נתן ברבי אושעיא's reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls that רב נתן ברבי אושעיא says the separated portion is real תרומה, and only the leftover produce is not fixed. This line opens a new question according to his view, and the question itself comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב נתן ברבי אושעיא, who said that 'he has done nothing' means only that the leftover produce is not fixed, but what he separated is תרומה, [what can be said?]
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next question. It brings up רב נתן ברבי אושעיא's narrower reading of 'he did nothing', and the actual question comes right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 20–25 explained the rulings according to רב חסדא, who says a separation made on purpose is completely worthless. Now the גמרא turns to רב נתן ברבי אושעיא from step 18, who holds that even an on-purpose separation is real תרומה and only fails to fix the leftovers. The difficulty his view raises is spelled out on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: He has done nothing. The ruling for someone who separates from impure produce for pure produce on purpose.
To fix the leftovers. To make the rest of the produce permitted to eat.
The leftover produce remaining after תרומה is taken.
It is תרומה. The separated part does take on holiness.

steps.confusionAlert: 'He has done nothing' does not mean the same thing to everyone. רב נתן ברבי אושעיא says it means only that the leftovers stay unfixed, while the separated part really is תרומה.

phrases.english: And according to רב נתן son of רבי אושעיא,
who said: "he has done nothing"
means for fixing the leftover produce,
but it is תרומה,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After working through the contradictions according to רב חסדא (steps 20–25), the גמרא turns to the other view, רב נתן ברבי אושעיא's from step 18, to raise a question against it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נתן ברבי אושעיא's reading that the separated portion is תרומה but the leftovers are not fixed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By רב נתן's view the separated portion is real תרומה, yet the leftovers are not fixed. The גמרא is about to question this view; the question itself is finished on the next amud.
